title: Genetics and Inheritance
seo_title: Year 10 Science: Genetics and Inheritance Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Explain the role of meiosis and mitosis and the function of chromosomes, DNA and genes in heredity and predict patterns of inheritance (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 10 science worksheets on genetics: DNA, genes and chromosomes, mitosis and meiosis, alleles, genotypes and phenotypes, Punnett squares, ratios and pedigrees. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Two alleles, one from each parent.
key_sub: Meiosis halves the chromosomes; fertilisation joins one allele from each parent.
body_html:
How to think about it

Genes are sections of DNA on chromosomes; we get one set from each parent.

  • Mitosis makes two identical body cells (growth, repair). Meiosis makes four gametes with half the chromosomes.
  • Each gene has alleles. Dominant (B) shows with one copy; recessive (b) shows only as bb.
  • A Punnett square predicts the chance of each genotype: Bb × Bb gives 1 BB : 2 Bb : 1 bb (3 : 1 phenotypes).
Example

Bb × Bb. Chance of bb?

Punnett square: BB, Bb, Bb, bb

Answer: 1 in 4 (25%)

Example

A cell has 46 chromosomes. A gamete has?

meiosis halves the number

Answer: 23

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up mitosis (identical body cells) and meiosis (gametes).
  • Thinking a dominant allele is the most common one.
  • Thinking a 3 : 1 ratio means exactly 3 of every 4 offspring.

faq.q: What is the difference between genotype and phenotype?
faq.a: The genotype is the alleles an organism has, such as Bb. The phenotype is the trait you can see, such as brown fur.

faq.q: Why are Punnett square results only probabilities?
faq.a: Which sperm fertilises which egg is random, so the real numbers of offspring only come close to the predicted ratio, especially in large samples.

faq.q: What is the difference between mitosis and meiosis?
faq.a: Mitosis makes two identical cells with the full set of chromosomes. Meiosis makes four different gametes with half the chromosomes.
